summary: Preinstall hook fetches Bun runtime to execute obfuscated in-package payload
details: package.json declares `"preinstall": "node setup.mjs"`. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime (pinned to oven-sh/bun v1.3.13 release zip) into a temp directory and then invokes `execFileSync(bunPath, [math_init.js])` against a co-shipped 727KB bundle. math_init.js is heavily obfuscated: a `// @bun @bun-cjs` tagged single-line file with hex-mangled identifiers, a large packed string array (`n7gIxM`) rotated by a shuffle function (`WV8StW`), and URLs reconstructed at runtime from fragments so no plain-text endpoint is visible. The package advertises itself as a Vue component for browsing assets and files; a UI library has no functional need for an install-time alternate-runtime dropper or an obfuscated Bun-executed payload. The declared `main` (`./dist/esm/Browser.js`) is not present in the tarball, further disconnecting the shipped install-time behavior from the advertised purpose. On `npm install`, the installer's host runs attacker-controlled code under a runtime that lies outside typical Node-based auditing tooling, with the executed content deliberately unreadable.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
